reuse.reason: Workers Think execution adapter. The official system-prompt registry is reused through its public entrypoint. Mounting or forking the official agent engine requires its Host session, sandbox and execution services; adapting only its Host seam cannot turn those execution semantics into Think durable submissions. This package explicitly implements the Think lifecycle and exposes mapped official session contracts; it does not claim native agent-engine equivalence. Session permission state is supplied by the separately forked official permission service, and effects read it at execution time. Official approval-policy context and switch notices are supplied by the Host at each actual model step. Installed Sessions persist non-human source:user-approval notices without waking inference. Stable IDs handle restart and private runtime provenance prevents duplicate delivery across SDK steps.
gaps: Think submission and compaction semantics differ from the official DSH agent loop; compatibility is verified at the session contract boundary.

Permission enforcement covers actual logical R2 model effects and action consent. It does not provide a POSIX process sandbox, arbitrary shell execution, or one-off filesystem escalation grants. Explicit user file edits use a separate service.

Legacy pending inputs without immutable execution-configuration evidence cannot safely resume. They fail closed with a visible error and retain a cancel/resubmit path; the current picker is never substituted.

Tool approval outside the Think WebSocket protocol requires its private _applyToolApproval transition because the installed SDK exports no public equivalent. The seam fails closed if absent; inference uses public continueLastTurn and actual response hooks. Durable intents prevent blind duplicate model calls, while provider effects remain subject to SDK recovery semantics.

Precise step/tool clocks and distinct requested/response model identifiers are available for new recorded executions. Unsupported imported timing or provider attribution remains unknown. Provider aggregate usage does not include a measured system/tools token split, so no character-count estimate is presented as accounting.

Approval policy notices are durable model context, not a replacement for native Agent inbox scheduling/cancellation or canonical command/notification UI history. No extra human input, model run or statistical turn is manufactured.
